reason: The text fragment (Exodus 2:11-15 in the Masoretic text) is a narrative account of Moses' early actions: witnessing an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, killing the Egyptian in secret, and subsequently fleeing Egypt when Pharaoh learns of his deed. Yahweh is not explicitly mentioned, referenced, or depicted anywhere in this passage. There is no characterization whatsoever of God as universal, omniscient, abstract, or possessing any other attributes. The passage is entirely a straightforward narrative of human events and actions without theological commentary about God's nature or divine attributes.
